name: US Maximum Pressure on Iran
description: Trump administration reimposed comprehensive sanctions after withdrawing from the JCPOA in May 2018. Targets Iran's oil exports, banking sector, and shipping. Biden maintained most sanctions. Severely disrupts INSTC routing through Iran and complicates IMEC's eastern connectivity.

name: Russia Post-Ukraine Invasion Sanctions
description: Unprecedented Western sanctions package imposed after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. Includes SWIFT disconnection of major banks, asset freezes, trade restrictions, and technology export bans. Reshapes Eurasian trade corridors as Russia pivots east toward China and India.
key_measures: Trade bans on luxury goods and key inputs
Flight bans and port access restrictions

name: Venezuela Oil and Financial Sanctions
description: Escalating sanctions targeting Venezuela's oil sector and financial system under both Trump and Biden administrations. Initially financial sector restrictions in 2017, expanded to oil embargo in 2019. Brief license relaxation in 2023 reversed in 2024. Forces Venezuelan crude into shadow fleet and alternative trade networks.

name: Syria Caesar Act Sanctions
description: Caesar Syria Civilian Protection Act imposes severe sanctions on anyone doing business with the Assad regime. Blocks reconstruction funding, energy sector investment, and military support. Complicates IMEC's Levant corridor routing and Iraq Development Road connectivity to Mediterranean ports.
key_measures: Secondary sanctions on foreign entities aiding Syria

name: China Technology and Chip Export Controls
description: October 2022 semiconductor export controls restrict China's access to advanced chips, chipmaking equipment, and AI technology. Expanded by Japan and Netherlands in 2023. Accelerates China's push for tech self-sufficiency and reshapes BRI investment toward strategic technology corridors.
key_measures: US person restrictions on supporting Chinese chip fabs

name: Cuba Comprehensive Embargo
description: Longest-standing comprehensive trade embargo in modern history. Prohibits virtually all US trade, financial transactions, and travel with Cuba. Codified by Helms-Burton Act (1996). Limited relevance to major corridor competition but demonstrates long-term economic warfare doctrine and affects Caribbean shipping lanes.

name: Qatar Blockade by Saudi-led Coalition
description: Saudi-led diplomatic and trade blockade of Qatar from June 2017 to January 2021. Severed land borders, airspace, and shipping access. Qatar pivoted to Turkey and Iran for supply routes. Resolved at Al-Ula summit. Demonstrated fragility of Gulf cooperation essential to IMEC corridor.

name: North Korea Maximum Pressure Sanctions
description: Multilateral UN sanctions regime progressively tightened since North Korea's first nuclear test in 2006. Among the most comprehensive in history, covering arms, trade, finance, shipping, and labor exports. Ship-to-ship transfers in East Asian waters complicate maritime corridor enforcement.

name: Myanmar Post-Coup Sanctions
description: Sanctions imposed after the February 2021 military coup targeting junta leaders, military conglomerates, and gem/timber sectors. China's BRI investments in Myanmar (Kyaukphyu deep-sea port, China-Myanmar Economic Corridor) continue despite Western sanctions, creating parallel economic governance.

name: Libya Sanctions Regime
description: UN sanctions imposed during 2011 civil war, maintained with modifications. Arms embargo remains in effect. Oil export restrictions lifted but governance disputes between rival governments create de facto trade uncertainty. Affects Mediterranean shipping lanes and North African corridor routing.

name: Sudan Conflict-Related Sanctions
description: Sanctions escalated after April 2023 civil war between SAF and RSF. Built on legacy of decades-long Sudan sanctions (partially lifted 2017). Targets military leaders, arms flows, and gold exports. Port Sudan on Red Sea is critical node for IMEC corridor and Horn of Africa trade.

name: Russia Energy Sector Sanctions - Oil Price Cap
description: $60/barrel price cap on Russian seaborne crude oil enforced through Western shipping insurance and services. Spawned massive shadow fleet of tankers operating outside Western insurance. Accelerated Russia-India oil trade via INSTC and Cape routes. Fundamentally restructured global tanker markets.

name: Iran Oil Buyer Secondary Sanctions
description: Secondary sanctions threatening to cut off any entity purchasing Iranian oil from the US financial system. China continues large-scale purchases through shadow mechanisms. India reduced purchases significantly, complicating INSTC corridor economics. Creates parallel financial architectures outside dollar system.

name: Houthi-Related Shipping Insurance Blacklists
description: War risk insurance surcharges and blacklists following Houthi attacks on Red Sea shipping since November 2023. Lloyd's Joint War Committee expanded high-risk zone. Forced massive rerouting around Cape of Good Hope, adding 10-14 days transit time. Existential threat to IMEC's Red Sea segment.
key_measures: Red Sea war risk insurance surcharges (0.5-1% hull value)
Cape of Good Hope rerouting advisories

name: Russia Nord Stream Pipeline Sanctions
description: US sanctions targeting Nord Stream 2 pipeline construction companies and certification bodies. CAATSA and PEESA legislation forced European contractors to withdraw. Pipeline completed but never certified. Destroyed by underwater explosions in September 2022. Demonstrated US willingness to weaponize sanctions against allied infrastructure projects. Sanctions became moot after the pipeline was destroyed by underwater explosions in September 2022.
